title: Is 0.999... equal to 1?
concept: 0.999... (9s forever) is exactly 1, shown through 1/3 = 0.333... and multiplying by 3.
kept: The question: equal to 1 or just very close
The friend's likely wrong answer (always a tiny gap) is offered as a guess option
The 1/3 = 0.333 times 3 argument as the main evidence
filled_in: Order of the experience (guess, slider of 3s, gap, why, shrink the gap, takeaway) since it was blank
A long-division table showing why 1/3 has endless 3s, to support the 1/3 = 0.333... step
A 'pick a gap size' step to show that any gap is beaten by enough 9s
Look and feel: plain digit tiles, blue for 3s and orange for 9s
The guess options are shown in a fixed order for every visitor; the page has no hidden versions

changed.what: The design's 0.333 times 3 on its own gives 0.999, which is not 1.
changed.why: A finite 0.333 is only close to 1/3. The page uses a slider for the number of 3s, shows the gap to 1 shrinking, and explains that the endless 3s make 1/3 exact.

math_check: All digits and gaps are computed with BigInt from k: nines = 10^k - 1, threes = nines/3 (exact, checked that 3 x threes = nines), gap = 1/10^k. The long-division table is computed by the loop r -> 10r mod 3. The gap-size step searches for the smallest n with 10^-n below the chosen gap. Checked by hand for k = 3 (0.333 x 3 = 0.999, gap 0.001) and the check script passed with no problems or warnings.
